items.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: I corrected a Beethoven thing, the Sonata, the “Moonlight Sonata,” I said why did he do that?

ctx.x: I did. I corrected a Beethoven thing, the Sonata, the “Moonlight Sonata,” I said why did he do that? He could have did this. He didn’t work within the rules. And Gershwin I did the same thing with. I said he’s doing contrary motion because of a rule when he doesn’t have to, he can do similar motion. [scats]
So why did he do that?
